p: Inside the Scottish Design Galleries, one piece deserves your full attention: Charles Rennie Mackintosh's Oak Room. Designed for Miss Cranston's tearooms on Ingram Street in Glasgow in 1907, it was taken apart and stored for decades before being painstakingly restored and rebuilt here. Stepping inside feels like time travel, and it's a must for anyone who loves Glasgow style.

It makes sense that this museum ended up in Dundee. The city was named the UK's first UNESCO City of Design in 2014, and its creative streak runs deep. It's the home of DC Thomson, publisher of The Beano, and you'll find bronze statues of Desperate Dan and Minnie the Minx in the city centre. Dundee also has a big video-game history: Lemmings and the original Grand Theft Auto were created by developers based here, so gamers will feel a connection.

Allow around one to two hours for the free galleries, longer if you add a ticketed exhibition. Dundee railway station is just across the road, making it easy to visit without the car. Spend some time on the waterfront afterwards, then head into town to the McManus, a free art gallery and museum in a handsome Gothic building. For a view of the whole city and the Tay, drive or climb up Dundee Law, the old volcanic hill that overlooks everything. On a clear day you can see right across to Fife.
